notToBeConfusedWith.name: Tequila
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Tequila is one specific style of mezcal, made only from blue agave in a defined region; mezcal is the wider category, usually pot-distilled from a roasted, often smoky, agave heart.

generalSubstitutes.note: Removes the smoke rather than replacing it; a drink built to carry a trace of mezcal alongside another spirit reads plainer and cleaner with tequila in its place.

forms.label: Standard
forms.sourceId: delmaguey.com/mezcal/vida (label strength, verified via retailer listing)
forms.sourceNote: Del Maguey Vida is taken as the reference bottle: it is the mezcal this drink's originating bar's recipe names by name, bottled at 42% alc./vol. (84 proof). The producer's own page returned a 403 on fetch, so the figure is cross-checked against a retailer's product listing quoting the same label strength rather than against the producer's site directly. No sugar or nutrition figure is published for it; mezcal is an unaged, unsweetened agave distillate, so sugarGPer100 is stated as 0 rather than omitted, but no fuller nutrition panel is available and none is estimated here. Density has no measured source and is taken from the density-classes.json 'spirit-40' class.
